overview: Knorr-Bremse AG is a Munich-headquartered global supplier of braking and other safety-relevant systems for rail and commercial vehicles, founded in 1905 [36][54]. It reported sales of about EUR 7.8bn at end-2025 and roughly 30,000 employees [54]. The Heinz Hermann Thiele Family Foundation indirectly holds 58.99% of shares, so ownership is concentrated [10].

Operational_Resilience_Score.evidence: Management describes a decentralized model that has kept the group resilient, but North American truck weakness and a planned production-footprint restructuring point to exposure [26][35][32].

Financial_Health_Score.evidence: Net debt fell 20% to EUR 1.3bn in 2025 and the 2025 order intake rose 12.5%, though the equity ratio dropped to 32.1% after the 2024 bond issue [6][26][8].

Quality_Risk_Score.evidence: No Knorr-Bremse-attributable quality incident is documented; the cited NHTSA recall names ZF North America as the component manufacturer [17][18].

Compliance_Risk_Score.evidence: A 2018 DOJ Sherman Act settlement over no-poach agreements imposed compliance obligations, and the company runs a compliance program and LkSG due diligence [13][14][16][46][47].

Credit_Rating_Score.evidence: S&P affirmed the A- long-term rating and revised the outlook to positive, and Moody's rated the 2024 bond A3 at issuance [38][39][41].

Safety_Incident_Score.evidence: The violation tracker lists nine minor safety-related records totalling about $80k, and no confirmed product-safety incident is attributed to Knorr-Bremse [15][18].

Sub_Tier_Visibility_Score.evidence: The company states it runs supplier risk assessments and on-site audits under the LkSG and is preparing for CSDDD, but sub-tier depth is not disclosed [47][49].

Geopolitical_Risk_Score.evidence: Tariff effects are cited as shaping order intake, and the company is exposed to North American truck cycles [26][35]; no sanctions-related exposure specific to Knorr-Bremse is documented [24][25].

Governance_Risk_Score.evidence: Family-foundation control and a supervisory board member who is also a management board member of the controlling family trust raise independence questions, although the board states it has enough independent members [9][10][12].

ESG_Performance_Score.evidence: The company publishes sustainability reports, follows ESG-linked investor engagement, and reports on EU Taxonomy alignment [1][2][3][4][47].

Environmental_Exposure_Score.evidence: The sources reviewed contain no quantified environmental incidents, emissions or permit exposures for Knorr-Bremse.

Labor_Stability_Score.evidence: The CFO said the company reduced its North American workforce [35], a historical plant closure was opposed by the works council [55], and a no-poach wage-suppression case was settled [50].

Digital_Security_Score.evidence: A dedicated cybersecurity competence centre at Selectron, a TCMS threat-detection product and no reported breach were found [28][29].

Political_Stability_Score.evidence: No source reviewed evaluates political stability risk for Knorr-Bremse's operating countries.

Industry_Benchmark_Score.evidence: The sources give no peer-group comparison for Knorr-Bremse's rating or margins.

Market_Sentiment_Score.evidence: The stock dipped after the Q2 2025 miss, and an analyst cut the target to EUR 76 and moved to HOLD [5][35].

Media_Sentiment_Score.evidence: Coverage is mixed: preliminary 2025 results were framed as higher profit, while the Q2 2025 miss and restructuring costs were reported negatively [26][32][35].

External_Intelligence_Score.evidence: Aggregated external signals combine a strong balance sheet with a past antitrust settlement, a shareholder-control question and a cyclical truck-market exposure [6][38][50][35].

# Supplier risk report: Knorr-Bremse AG

*Researched 2026-10-18 15:29 · 55 sources · 3 dig-deeper round(s) · verdict: **approve with conditions***

Knorr-Bremse AG is a Munich-headquartered global supplier of braking and other safety-relevant systems for rail and commercial vehicles, founded in 1905 [36][54]. It reported sales of about EUR 7.8bn at end-2025 and roughly 30,000 employees [54]. The Heinz Hermann Thiele Family Foundation indirectly holds 58.99% of shares, so ownership is concentrated [10].

**Total Risk Index (dataset formula): 38 (Medium)**, riskier than 18% of the 10,000 suppliers in the dataset. Evidence covers 78% of the index weight; dimensions without evidence are set to the dataset average. Range **33–44** if the unknown dimensions sit anywhere between the dataset's 10th and 90th percentile.

## Recommendation
Approve with conditions. The balance sheet and credit rating are sound, and the 2018 no-poach matter is closed with the compliance obligations settled [13][38][50]. Before award, ask for evidence of the antitrust compliance programme's current scope and the auditor-verified 2025 results once published [33]. Ask for the scope of the EUR 30m restructuring and whether it affects the plants supplying your programme [32]. Also request sub-tier supplier mapping under LkSG [47] and confirmation of the governance arrangements following the family foundation's control [10][9].

## Red flags
- **DOJ no-poach antitrust settlement and follow-on employee class action** (severity 3/5, confirmed · confirmed): In April 2018 the DOJ settled with Knorr-Bremse and Wabtec over no-poach agreements under Sherman Act s.1 [13][14][16]. The follow-on class action settled in February 2020 for $48.95m total, with Knorr paying $12m [50]. Violation Tracker lists a $12m competition-related penalty [15]. [[13]](https://www.frankllp.com/resources/investigations/rail-equipment-manufacturers-no-poach-agreements-antitrust-inves) [[14]](https://www.justice.gov/opa/press-release/file/1048481/dl) [[16]](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2018/04/16/2018-07840/united-states-v-knorr-bremse-ag-and-westinghouse-air-brake-technologies-corporation-proposed-final) [[50]](https://www.lieffcabraser.com/2020/02/lieff-cabraser-announces-settlement-of-knorr-and-wabtec-employee-no-poach-antitrust-lawsuit) [[15]](https://violationtracker.goodjobsfirst.org/parent/knorr-bremse)
- **Q2 2025 earnings miss on weak North American truck market** (severity 2/5, confirmed · confirmed): Q2 2025 results missed forecasts and the stock dipped [35]. The CFO acknowledged North American workforce reductions [35]. Source [5] cuts the target to EUR 76 and downgrades to HOLD, but its title refers to Q3 2024 results, so it does not clearly support the Q2 2025 linkage. The size of the miss is not stated. [[35]](https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-knorrbremse-q2-2025-misses-forecasts-stock-dips-93CH-4165639) [[5]](https://downloads.research-hub.de/2024%2011%2001%20Knorr%20Bremse%20Q3%2024%20results___w7c5krgy.pdf)
- **Restructuring costs of up to EUR 30m for production footprint** (severity 2/5, confirmed · confirmed): With preliminary, unaudited 2025 figures, Knorr-Bremse said it may incur restructuring costs of up to EUR 30m to optimise its global production footprint [32][33][34]. Final figures are due with the annual report. [[32]](https://thebrakereport.com/knorr-bremse-achieves-higher-profit-and-profitability-in-2025) [[33]](https://newsroom.knorr-bremse.com/en/knorr-bremse-on-course-for-success-with-higher-profit-and-profitability) [[34]](https://www.eqs-news.com/news/corporate/knorr-bremse-on-course-for-success-with-higher-profit-and-profitability/a384fcaa-3051-4aa1-8ea3-b70de97379a6_en)

## Checked and refuted
- **Balance sheet leverage up and S&P rating downgrade**: S&P affirmed A- [38] and revised outlook to positive [39]. Net debt fell 20% to EUR 1.3bn in 2025 [6]. A downgrade appears in [7], but the rating has since recovered with no remaining exposure. [[6]](https://fiscal.ai/company/XETR_KBX/metrics/ratios/net-debt) [[7]](https://www.spglobal.com/ratings/en/regulatory/article/-/view/sourceId/12866459) [[38]](https://cbonds.com/news/3180761) [[39]](https://www.spglobal.com/ratings/en/regulatory/article/-/view/type/HTML/id/1428256)
- **Brake chamber recall (Nova Bus, 2,090 units)**: NHTSA recall 24V-559 names ZF North America as supplier of the Knorr-Bresme 20/22-57 brake chamber, citing a manufacturing defect at ZF [17][18]. Not attributed to Knorr-Bremse. [[17]](https://thebrakereport.com/brake-chamber-recall-affects-2090-units) [[18]](https://static.nhtsa.gov/odi/rcl/2024/RCLRPT-24V559-8397.PDF)

## Strengths
- A- rating affirmed with positive outlook [38][39].
- Net debt down 20% to EUR 1.3bn in 2025 [6].
- 2025 order intake up 12.5%, with the company citing decentralized resilience [26].
- Dedicated cybersecurity competence centre and threat-detection product for TCMS [28][29].
- Formal LkSG due-diligence processes and CSDDD preparation [47].
